classification.difficultyReason: Choose corresponding graph features such as vertices, crossings or asymptotes, measure the displacement, and express its direction correctly in function notation.

content.prompt: For each pair of graphs, find the equation of $y=g(x)$ in terms of $f(x)$.

spec.description: Matching upward-opening parabolas in one coordinate plane, with vertices at (0,-4) and (0,1); no grid. Red identifies f and blue identifies g. The curves use the same quadratic Bezier geometry translated vertically.
spec.mathematics: The minimum rises from -4 to 1 without horizontal displacement or change of shape.
spec.answerVisibility: Both labelled curves are permanent givens; the equation beneath the source figure is answer-only.

answer.worked:
The minimum moves from $(0,-4)$ to $(0,1)$, so the graph translates up $5$ units. Replace $y$ with $y-5$:
$$\begin{aligned}y-5&=f(x)\\y&=f(x)+5.\end{aligned}$$
Hence $g(x)=f(x)+5$.

spec.description: Matching increasing concave-down curves with continuation arrows, no grid and no explicit asymptote. The red curve passes through (-2,0) and (0,2); the blue curve is its exact four-unit downward translation.
spec.mathematics: Corresponding y-intercepts are 2 and -2. The shared qualitative Bezier path is translated without changing its control geometry; no base equation is asserted.
spec.answerVisibility: Both curves and their labels are givens; the supplied function equation is answer-only.

answer.worked:
The $y$-intercept moves from $2$ to $-2$, so the graph translates down $4$ units. Replace $y$ with $y+4$:
$$\begin{aligned}y+4&=f(x)\\y&=f(x)-4.\end{aligned}$$
Hence $g(x)=f(x)-4$.

spec.description: Two reciprocal-shaped graphs, each with both branches and continuation arrows. The y-axis is their shared vertical asymptote. The blue horizontal asymptote is dashed at y=-1; the red horizontal asymptote is the x-axis.
spec.mathematics: The blue graph is exactly one unit below the red graph and crosses the x-axis at 3. Reciprocal plotting uses the coefficient determined by these displayed features, without printing an additional base equation.
spec.answerVisibility: Curves, legends and dashed asymptote are givens; the supplied function equation is answer-only.

answer.worked:
The horizontal asymptote moves from $y=0$ to $y=-1$, so the graph translates down $1$ unit. Replace $y$ with $y+1$:
$$\begin{aligned}y+1&=f(x)\\y&=f(x)-1.\end{aligned}$$
Hence $g(x)=f(x)-1$.

spec.description: Matching increasing S-shaped curves, red flattening at (3,0) and blue flattening at (-4,0). Both have continuation arrows; no grid. A common qualitative Bezier curve is translated horizontally and clipped to the displayed coordinate window.
spec.mathematics: The blue graph is the same shape translated seven units left. The red y-intercept is near -4 and the blue y-intercept near 5; no explicit polynomial equation is supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: Both curves and their labels are givens; the supplied function equation is answer-only.

answer.worked:
The flattened crossing moves from $(3,0)$ to $(-4,0)$, a translation $7$ units left. Replace $x$ with $x+7$:
$$g(x)=f(x+7).$$

spec.description: Matching increasing logarithmic-shaped curves, red crossing (-5,0) and blue crossing (1,0), with steep lower branches and continuation arrows at both ends. No grid or separately drawn asymptotes. A common qualitative Bezier path is translated exactly six units.
spec.mathematics: The red curve has its suggested domain boundary at x=-6; the blue curve has its suggested domain boundary at x=0. No logarithm base or explicit base equation is asserted.
spec.answerVisibility: Both curves and their labels are givens; the supplied function equation is answer-only.

answer.worked:
The $x$-intercept moves from $-5$ to $1$, a translation $6$ units right. Replace $x$ with $x-6$:
$$g(x)=f(x-6).$$
